OpenClaw's only, as a plan CLI runs unmodified), holder (name@version), path (a directory ending in / or one file, relative to the package, outside node_modules/), why (what shows it is never loaded)}; an image record accepts only an advisory Debian has not fixed)}. bundled (#5853): copies of a library that a guest's pinned binary links statically, which no lockfile or Debian scan reads, {holder (the pinned download, name@version), copy (library@version), build (the script that pins it, and checks the copy where it can), issue (an open issue), ids (the advisories accepted against the copy), why (how the copy was identified, and each advisory's reach)}; `vulncheck.py run` queries OSV for each copy at its upstream release tag (#5873) and reads its upstream release notes for the CVEs fixed after that release (#5888); an advisory from either fails unless ids names it or an alias, and an id neither lists is reported as info.

bundled.why: The nodejs.org linux-x64 build links OpenSSL 3.5.9 statically (its string "OpenSSL 3.5.9 29 Sep 2026"; build-rootfs.sh checks process.versions.openssl against this record). The five 2026-11-10 fixes and the two 2026-11-17 ones exist only as commits on OpenSSL's openssl-3.5 branch (its CHANGES.md lists no 3.5.10 release yet), and no node release carries them (nodejs.org/dist/index.json, checked 2026-11-17: v24.22.3 and v26.13.1, the latest LTS releases, both list 3.5.9). Reach, against each fix commit: -88822 (1a73dc5) is BIO_dgram_detect_peer_addr returning uninitialised stack bytes for a non-IPv4 peer; node has no DTLS or OpenSSL QUIC and makes no datagram BIO, and node:quic uses ngtcp2, is off by default, and no file of the OpenClaw install imports it. -95691 (f624467) is a use-after-free in OpenSSL's QUIC record layer, which node never uses. -107496 (a0051cf) is EC key generation looping forever on a group of order 1; node generates EC keys only on named curves (generateKeyPair('ec', {namedCurve}), createECDH(name)) and TLS ECDHE uses only named groups. -95692 (257a342) needs a GCM-SIV IV other than 12 bytes, which createCipheriv refuses (src/crypto/crypto_cipher.cc at v24.22.3). -88823 (159e1de) is a zero-length AAD update dropping the AAD gathered so far, and a reinitialised context keeping stale AAD; the first is reachable from JS (setAAD with an empty buffer on aes-*-gcm-siv) and node never reinitialises a cipher context, but no file of the OpenClaw install names GCM-SIV (its createCipheriv and createDecipheriv calls use aes-*-gcm, aes-128-cbc, aes-128-ecb and des-ede), koffi binds only libc and libsystemd functions, and none of its linux-x64 .node addons imports an OpenSSL symbol from node. Code the agent runs in the guest can reach the GCM-SIV flaws only in its own process, which it already controls. -124709 (f3acb0a, ssl/quic) is a QUIC server keeping a rejected stream's state after the peer resets it; it lives in OpenSSL's own QUIC stack, which node never creates (no OSSL_QUIC_*_method or SSL_new_listener in src/ at v24.22.3; node:quic is ngtcp2 over OpenSSL's TLS, off by default, and no file of the OpenClaw install imports it). -35190 (9491b0d, tls_parse_ctos_key_share) is a TLS 1.3 server reading past a fixed group list when the Suite B flag is set, which SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags or a cipher string starting SUITEB128 or SUITEB192 does (ssl_ciph.c check_suiteb_cipher_list), so node's ciphers option, --tls-cipher-list and an openssl.cnf CipherString can set it; nothing in the guest does: no file of the OpenClaw install names SUITEB, the guest sets no NODE_OPTIONS, OPENSSL_CONF or openssl.cnf, the install's ciphers uses are client-side passthroughs, and the gateway serves plain HTTP on loopback. Clears with a node release that bundles the fixes (#6075).

The static musl binaries vendor/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/bin/codex and codex-code-mode-host each link three crypto libraries: OpenSSL 3.6.4 (built by openssl-sys 0.9.111 for openssl 0.10.75 and native-tls 0.2.14; string "OpenSSL 3.6.4 25 Aug 2026"), AWS-LC 5.7.0 (aws-lc-rs 1.18.1) and ring 0.17.14, the last two for rustls 0.23.45. Their three GCM-SIV spellings are OpenSSL's default-provider name table. OpenSSL 3.6.5 (2026-09-29) fixes the first 13 ids (openssl-3.6/CHANGES.md); the last five are the 2026-11-10 advisories, branch commits with no release yet. No codex release links a fixed OpenSSL: every stable linux-x64 release from 0.163.0 to 0.169.0 (npm latest, checked 2026-11-16) holds the same 3.6.4 string, so the pin bump waits on #5894. Reach: the CLI makes no TLS connection on the guest's run path. base_url and chatgpt_base_url are plain HTTP to the in-worker forwarder on 127.0.0.1, the only route out (guest/codex/ASSUMPTIONS.md C18; the egress proxy outside the guest does the TLS), and tools run with no network (C3). So no peer certificate reaches X.509 parsing (-35189, CRLDP heap growth) and no handshake runs at all. Apart from that, the only openssl crate sources the binaries name are bio.rs, error.rs, ssl/bio.rs and ssl/mod.rs, native-tls's TLS client over TCP through the crate's own stream BIO: it never calls SSL_set_SSL_CTX, a server-side SNI switch (-72897); it has no DTLS (-84782, -75806) and no datagram BIO calling BIO_dgram_detect_peer_addr (-88822); OpenSSL's QUIC (-35191, -42772, -54873, -75804, -84784, -95691) is reached only through OSSL_QUIC_client_method, which native-tls does not use (the binaries' QUIC is quinn over rustls); nothing calls OpenSSL's CMP client (-75805); nothing signs with OpenSSL, so neither the generic-curve ECDSA/SM2 nonce timing (-54872) nor SM2 signing (-77696) is reached, and -54875 affects only ARM64 and RISC-V builds, not this x86_64 one; TLS has no GCM-SIV suite (-88823, -95692); and ECDHE generates keys only on named groups (-107496). CODEX_INTEGRITY pins the tarball's bytes, so the copy changes only with a new pin, and build-rootfs.sh fails unless each binary holds one OpenSSL version string, this record's copy (#5873). Clears with a codex release that links a fixed OpenSSL (#5894).

The flaw is a double free in regcomp/regexec (re_dfa_add_node, build_range_exp, match_ctx_add_entry) after a failed realloc, CWE-415 (CVE-2026-100290, GLIBC-SA-2026-0028, CVSS 3.7 AV:N/AC:H/A:L; glibc 2.3 to 2.44): reached only under memory pressure, and the expected impact is a crash. Image package glibc 2.41-12+deb13u4 (libc-bin, libc6, libc6-dev). The flaw is a double free in glob() (CWE-415, CVE-2026-126765, GLIBC-SA-2026-0032, CVSS 3.7 AV:N/AC:H/A:L; glibc 2.44 and earlier): when an allocation fails while glob prepends the directory name to the names it matched, the names already rewritten are freed but stay in the result vector, and globfree frees them again. It is reached only when the calling process is already near its memory limit and the attacker can make the match set large enough to exhaust it, by controlling the pattern and knowing the filesystem layout. Reach (#6285), from the dynamic imports and NEEDED closure of every ELF file in the main tree image.yml builds (image/import_sweep.py, held to import_sweep.allow [glob], which fails the build on a new importer): agentOS's own binaries are static Go built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and link no glibc; bash expands patterns with its own code. Seven files import glob, glob64 or wordexp (glibc's caller of glob): libsystemd-shared, whose one call (safe_glob, systemd 257.13) expands patterns from root-owned configuration only: unit settings in PID 1 and systemd-executor (EnvironmentFile=, ImportCredential=, PathExistsGlob=, ConditionPathExistsGlob=; no agentOS process starts a transient unit), the conditions of networkd's and udevd's .network, .netdev and .link files, sysctl.d and tmpfiles.d entries, and journalctl --file and systemd-analyze's command line; iproute2's ip, whose one glob is the fixed /proc/[0-9]*/fd/[0-9]* of ip tuntap show; libnftables, globbing a ruleset's include path, and nft loads only rulesets agentOS renders, which hold none, or root-owned files; libpopt, globbing only in its config readers, which cryptsetup, integritysetup and veritysetup never call; and pam_access, pam_limits and pam_namespace, globbing their /etc/security config directories. The 113 other files reaching it do so through those libraries, almost all through libsystemd-shared (journald, logind, resolved, networkd, udevd and systemd's tools), whose call sites are the ones named. No pattern comes from the network or from a guest. The sweep also reads static copies of glibc and dlsym lookups by name (#6298): ldconfig, static, carries glob() for the include patterns of root-owned /etc/ld.so.conf; llama-server and agentos-camdecode, which link libc.a, carry no glob, regex or wide scanf code. Since #6299 it also reads lookups through a library's dlsym wrapper and glibc code embedded in dynamic files, fails on packed files, holds every glibc it reads to the marks, and pins each reviewed file by SHA-256: libpam, libselinux, libmount and libcrypto, read to pass dlsym only fixed names (libcrypto's caller-name exports count as lookups themselves), are no lookup source, so libsystemd-core's assert(glob) text is no lookup and it reaches glob() only through safe_glob above; no dynamic file embeds a copy and none is packed. OSV lists no fixed version for Debian 12, 13 or 14 (2.41-12+deb13u5 is listed as affected), and the image already takes live security.debian.org, so neither a rebuild nor a snapshot bump clears it. libc-bin is Essential and every Essential package depends on libc6, so neither can be purged. Fails again once Debian ships one.

Guest package glibc (libc6, libc6-dev), also in the main tree, whose image record accepts the same advisory and gives the flaw. The guests' files ship in the main tree under /usr/lib/agentos/images, which image/import_sweep.py reads on every build (#6285): no file there imports or reaches glob, glob64 or wordexp (each guest's bash expands patterns with its own code), and a new one fails the build until import_sweep.allow [glob] and this record name it. It also reads static copies of glibc and dlsym lookups by name (#6298): bwrap's static libc carries no glob, and the codex binaries link musl, not glibc. The openclaw guest's node imports dlsym and holds "glob" only as its JavaScript fs.glob API name (implemented over readdir); its dlsym calls look up fixed addon entry names, and import_sweep.allow [glob] names it. Were a program the agent runs to reach it, the double free needs that process near its memory limit and stays inside the guest sandbox. Debian 13 has no fix. Fails again once Debian ships one.
